teaser: Write the article first, then send five agent readers through it: a catalogue, an ontology and maps, the arc, two minutes, and a deck.
core_idea: Long, evidence-rich articles are hard to consume, and the answer is not shorter articles but extraction after the writing: the prose stays the source because writing is how the argument is found, and five agent readers with defined roles then produce other views of it, two building the platform (a Librarian that catalogues every item with its verbatim anchor, a Cartographer that builds an ontology at article, topic and site altitude and draws the maps) and three writing for a person (a Historian on what the article added and where it sits, an Explainer in two minutes, a Storyteller as a deck); run on five articles it catalogued 662 items, flagged 32 problems in published text, merged ideas named differently across articles, and measured each article's contribution as new concepts falling 17, 11, 5, 11, 1.

quotes.text: It does not change how the writing is done. It maximises what the writing produces.
quotes.why: The design rule: extraction after the prose, not a new way of writing.

quotes.text: a topic ontology tells you what is new to the topic; only a site ontology tells you what is new.
